# wt / fuzz-eval

wt's own fuzz target `fuzz-eval` ([source](source/fuzz-eval.C), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over wt (emweb/wt at 0ec92b6b).

Copies the input (Size from 10 to 5120 bytes) into a string and evaluates it as a plural-case expression with n = 0 through Wt::WMessageResources::evalPluralCase, catching and dropping WInvalidFormatException and WInvalidOperationException, and drops the result. It returns -1 for an input with Size below 10 or above 5120.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against wt at commit 0ec92b6b.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified: source/fuzz-eval.C is wt 0ec92b6b's fuzz/fuzz-eval.C with one Theorem Labs change: its length check returns -1, not 1, for an input outside its limits (libFuzzer rejects the input; the driver exits 0, not 78).

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends.
